profile.address: 120 East Van Buren Street, Phoenix, AZ 85004
profile.reading:
QTS Phoenix 1, which the company codes PHX1, occupies 288,000 square feet at 120 East Van Buren Street in downtown Phoenix, of which 108,000 square feet is raised floor. QTS gives the site 32 MW of utility power capacity. QTS does not own the building: 120 East Van Buren is the Phoenix carrier hotel, owned by Digital Realty, and several operators lease space in it, LightEdge and AIS among them. QTS came by the operation through its acquisition of Carpathia Hosting in 2015.

The distinction QTS draws in its own datasheet is worth keeping. Thirty-two megawatts is the utility service the building can draw, not the IT load its customers run, and the two are not the same number. Directories that list 32 MW as this facility capacity are repeating the utility figure without the qualifier. QTS publishes no IT load for PHX1, so this registry records none.

The electrical plant is described in more detail than most operators offer. There are seventeen generator positions, of which nine hold generators of various sizes and eight are sited and available for more. Bulk diesel storage runs to 10,500 gallons with 80,000 gallons permitted and sited, and there is space set aside for tenants to install their own generators, fuel and UPS. Cooling is two 1,000-ton towers with a third position sited. That pattern, capacity present but deliberately unfilled, is what a carrier-hotel operator builds when it expects tenants to arrive with their own requirements.

For accelerator computing this is a connectivity site rather than a capacity site. A downtown retrofit sharing a building with other operators is not where a large training cluster goes. The value here is that 120 East Van Buren is the best connected building in Phoenix, which matters for inference close to users and for interconnection between networks. QTS's own large Phoenix capacity sits about four miles east on its 40th Street campus, a separate five building, 80 acre site this registry tracks as its own facility rather than as part of this Van Buren suite. QTS's current site for that campus states it delivers more than 210 MW of critical capacity across its five buildings combined, a figure describing the whole campus rather than any single building in it. An earlier trade press account of that campus's groundbreaking cited a larger planned figure near 280 MW for eventual full buildout, a forward looking construction target this registry has not reconciled with the current 210 MW figure, since neither source clarifies whether the two describe the same measurement at different points in the campus's buildout.
